To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the test suites that use CSS selectors have the lowest maintenance effort, followed by the test suites that employ XPath and finally the ones that use the name property of HTML elements.
the test suite maintainability of a web application depends on the type of locators employed in the test suite and on the type of web elements that are used to locate the elements.

(1) the number of locators in a test suite has a significant impact on the maintainability of that suite; (2) the number of different locators in a suite is a good indicator of its maintainability; (3) the number of unique locators in a page is a good indicator for the number of loca-tors needed for that page.

the problem of how to maintain test suites in order to reduce the time and effort spent on test maintenance and increase the quality and reliability of test suites.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need to develop and maintain test suites that are easy to maintain.
the use of CSS selectors is the most maintainable approach, while XPath is less maintainable and the use of ID is the most brittle approach.
the use of XPath locators in the test cases is more expensive than the use of CSS locators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the use of CSS selectors is the most effective locator type for the maintenance of the Selenium WebDriver test suite, followed by XPath, and the least effective is the use of ID locators.
, in the case study, the test suites employing XPath locators are more maintainable than test suites employing CSS and ID locators.
we are comparing the maintainability of test suites employing different types of locators.

using CSS locators in test cases can be a good alternative to XPath locators.
, in general, XPath-based locators tend to be more maintainable than CSS-based ones.
